typescript-eslint 8.70.1 reports `void` as a call's type argument: no-invalid-void-type lists CallExpression among the grandparents where `void` under a TSTypeParameterInstantiation stays invalid even with allowInGenericTypeArguments true (packages/eslint-plugin/src/rules/no-invalid-void-type.ts, invalidGrandParents; its test reports `functionGeneric<void>(undefined);`), while `new Promise<void>()` and a tagged template's type argument are allowed. The steer to pass undefined instead is wrong for a call: `Promise.withResolvers<undefined>()` makes every `resolve()` need an argument, and a type test's `toEqualTypeOf<void>()` asserts a different type with undefined. Rerail allows `void` as any call's type argument while allowInGenericTypeArguments is true, and still reports it under false or the array form.

The line before carries `// eslint-disable-next-line jest/no-focused-tests`, which names another plugin's rule, so ESLint reports the `test.only`. The port carries `suppress.oxlint` `no-focused-tests` (Oxlint 1.88.0 implements it, reads `eslint-disable` comments and matches a directive name with a `/` by its part after the last `/`), so the comment silences it as it silences Oxlint, by design (docs/pack-format.md, check 4). Without the comment the port reports the `test.only`, as ESLint does.
